subtitles.text: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal. LeetCode one oh two.
Given the root of a binary tree, return its values level by level, from top to bottom, left to right.
For this tree, that's three. Then nine and twenty. Then four, seven, fifteen, eight. Then six and two.
Depth first search dives straight down one branch, so it visits the nodes in the wrong order.
We want to sweep across each level before going deeper. That's breadth first search.
And breadth first search runs on a queue. First in, first out.
The trick is to measure the queue's length at the start of each level. Exactly that many nodes belong to it.
Let's run it. The queue starts with just the root.
Level zero. The queue holds one node. Pop three, record it, and push nine and twenty.
Level one. Two nodes. Pop nine, push four and seven. Pop twenty, push fifteen and eight.
Level two holds four nodes. Pop them in order. Seven brings six, and fifteen brings two.
Level three. Six and two have no children, so nothing new joins the queue.
The queue is empty, and we have all four levels.
Each node goes in and out of the queue once, so the time is linear.
The queue holds at most one full level, so the space is the width of the tree.
One queue, and one snapshot of its size per level.
Sweep level by level, and the tree comes out in rows.
